memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Laban and Bethuel answered, 'This is from the LORD; we can say nothing to you one way or the other. Here is Rebekah; take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has directed.'" - Gen 24:50-51 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The family listens to the whole account and reaches a simple conclusion: "This is from the Lord." The evidence is too clear to argue with. When God's hand is unmistakable, the wisest response is to yield to it rather than resist.

There are seasons when God's leading becomes plain — circumstances line up, His Word confirms a direction, and wise counsel agrees. In such moments, we are not called to keep debating but to say, as Laban and Bethuel did, "as the LORD has directed." Recognising God's leading brings a settled peace.

Of course, we must be careful. Not everything that goes smoothly is automatically God's will, and this family's discernment came after hearing a clear testimony rooted in prayer. But there is a beautiful humility in people who are willing to submit their plans when they see God at work. They released Rebekah rather than clinging to her.

Is there an area where God has already made His direction clear, yet you keep hesitating? Sometimes faith simply means agreeing with what God is obviously doing and stepping forward. When the Lord directs, let your heart say yes.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an area where God's direction is clear, yet I keep hesitating?
2. Am I willing to yield my plans when I see God at work?
3. How do I discern God's leading — through His Word, prayer, and counsel?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when Your direction is clear, give me the humility to say yes without delay. Help me to recognise Your hand and follow where You lead. Amen.
